newsitem.title: VIETNAM: U.N. chides Vietnam on maternal mortality record.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chides Vietnam on maternal mortality record.

text.p: The U.N. Children's Fund said on Tuesday that Vietnam had failed to reduce the rate of maternal mortality, and called on the government for less rhetoric and more action to resolve the problem.
"Every day, seven Vietnamese women die in pregnancy or delivery," UNICEF quoted its Vietnam representative, Rima Saleh, as telling a workshop in Hanoi last week.
"What we need today are not words, but actions. We know the situation and we know the solutions," she said.
UNICEF said that in 1990, the government set a target of reducing the maternal mortality rate from 160 to 70 deaths per 100,000 live births by 2000.
"However, and despite the lack of official data, it seems that no progress has been made in seven years," UNICEF said in a statement.
"It is time for the government to give much stronger priority, in terms of human and financial investments, on safe motherhood if the target is to be reached," it said.
It said the root causes of maternal mortality included a lack of access to appropriate health care, the low status of women in society, especially ethnic minorities, and poverty.

UNICEF said 75 percent of women in Vietnam did not receive maternal care, either becasuse they did not have access to health services or because they were not informed about the importance of prenatal consultation.
